title: Does Benign Fine-Tuning Degrade Refusal Through Shared Components? A Targeted Probe

original_idea.body:
# Does Benign Fine-Tuning Degrade Refusal Through Shared Components?

**Problem:** Unclear whether refusal degradation is proportional to how much the fine-tuning task overlaps the refusal mechanism.

**Direction:** LoRA fine-tune a small safety-tuned model on benign datasets varying in task type, measure refusal rate after each.

**Why it matters:** Gives an actionable warning that certain task types are riskier.

**Relevant context:** arXiv:2510.21885; arXiv:2510.07775.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Identifying which benign task types most erode refusal gives an actionable warning.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: LoRA fine-tunes on varied benign datasets plus refusal eval; guided.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused task-type comparison; needs several benign datasets and fine-tunes.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open models, public data; weak lab incentive on task-type erosion mapping.

low_compute.reasoning: Several small LoRA fine-tunes on a 1B model; one GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Benign fine-tuning erosion known; the task-type/overlap dependence may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Erosion known; task-type overlap dependence may be open.
